label: conj:yang-mills-mass-gap
title: Yang--Mills Existence and Mass Gap
html:
Conjecture (Yang–Mills existence and mass gap, categorical formulation). Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe over a commutative ring R with substrate parameter q > 1. Let \nabla be a categorical connection on the Frobenius–Hopf object A with curvature F_\nabla = \nabla^2. Let \mathfrak{S}_q[\nabla] be the q-weighted Yang–Mills–Levi functional. Let \Omega_0 \colon R \to \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A) be the vacuum state — the unique G_q-invariant functional on the direct limit algebra \mathcal{A}_\infty = \varinjlim \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n).

Then:

  1. Existence. There exists a connection \nabla that is a critical point of \mathfrak{S}_q[\nabla] (a categorical Yang–Mills connection). The vacuum state \Omega_0 extends to a positive-definite sesquilinear form on the Hilbert completion \overline{\mathcal{A}_\infty}, defining a physical Hilbert space \mathcal{H}_q.

  2. Mass gap. Every non-vacuum excitation \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A in the spectrum of the categorical transfer matrix \mathcal{T}_q \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) \to \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) satisfies

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)  \geq  \Delta_q  >  0,

where \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) is the categorical mass and \Delta_q is a strictly positive constant depending only on q and the Frobenius–Hopf structure of A. Equivalently, the two-point function

  \bigl\langle
  \tau(\varrho(t)),
  \tau(\varrho(0))
  \bigr\rangle_{\Omega_0}
   \sim 
  \sum_{n \geq 0}
  A_n \exp\!\bigl(-\Delta_n t\bigr)
  \qquad (t \to \infty)

has \Delta_0 = \Delta_q > 0. There is no massless excitation above the vacuum.

Translation from the classical problem. The classical Yang–Mills millennium problem asks for the existence of a quantum Yang–Mills theory on \mathbb{R}^4 with compact simple gauge group G, satisfying the Wightman axioms, and having a strictly positive mass gap \Delta > 0 in the energy spectrum.

In the QOU framework, the translation is:

See Table.

Naturality of the categorical setting. The mass gap is a topological consequence of the Frobenius–Hopf structure. The categorical mass \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) is computed via the trace-norm through the comultiplication \Delta. The topological decomposition shows that every non-trivial vortex acquires at least one crossing energy \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) > 0 from the Skein relation. The mass gap is bounded below by the minimum crossing energy:

  \Delta_q
   \geq 
  \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) \cdot (q - 1)^2
  = 
  \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})(q - 1)^2
   >  0
  \quad\text{for all } q > 1.

The positivity of \Delta_q for q > 1 is the categorical shadow of confinement. The deformation parameter q \neq 1 breaks the classical conformal symmetry that would allow massless excitations. The Skein relation forces every non-trivial braid word to carry strictly positive crossing energy.

The \mathbb{G}_m-torsion obstruction. The mass gap is a regular function on \mathbb{G}_m = \mathrm{Spec}\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. It vanishes precisely on the 2-torsion subgroup \mu_2 = \{1, -1\}, and is strictly positive on the non-torsion locus (1, \infty) \subset \mathbb{G}_m(\mathbb{R}). The not-root-of-unity axiom ensures q \notin \mu_\infty, placing the substrate parameter in the region where the gap is positive.

The Kummer filtration of the obstruction space H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) provides the common algebraic framework. The mass gap and the classical limit obstruction both reduce to divisibility of \chi(A) in the Kummer tower. Since \chi(A) = -6 for the Descartes universe, the obstruction is one-dimensional and persists at all primes > 3.

Relation to confinement. In the archimedean realisation, the mass gap implies that the lightest glueball (the simplest non-trivial closed vortex \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A with no quark endpoints) has mass \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{glue}} \geq \Delta_q > 0. Isolated colour charges would require a vortex of infinite length (and hence infinite mass). Confinement follows: all finite-energy excitations are colour singlets.
